code: function burnProducts( ProductBurn[] calldata products ) external { uint256 totalEarned; uint256 totalPositions; uint256 fee; for (uint256 i = 0; i < products.length; i++) { uint256 balanceBefore = collateral.balanceOf(address(this)); IVault(products[i].vault).burnBatch(products[i].products); uint256 balanceAfter = collateral.balanceOf(address(this)); uint256 earned = balanceAfter - balanceBefore; totalEarned += earned; bytes32 id = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(products[i].vault, products[i].products[0].expiry, products[i].products[0].anchorPrices)); totalPositions += _positions[id]; if (earned > _positions[id]) { fee += (earned - _positions[id]) * IFeeCollector(feeCollector).tradingFeeRate() / 1e18; } delete _positions[id]; } if (fee > 0) { totalFee += fee; totalEarned -= fee; } if (totalEarned > totalPositions) { totalCollateral += totalEarned - totalPositions; } else if (totalEarned < totalPositions) { totalCollateral -= totalPositions - totalEarned; } emit ProductsBurned(products, totalCollateral, fee); }
vulnerability: Cost basis deletion and totalCollateral inflation due to non-unique position ID and first-product-only accounting
reason: The position ID used in _positions is keccak256(vault, expiry, anchorPrices). It ignores collateralAtRiskPercentage and isMaker, so multiple products can share the same ID and their cost bases are aggregated. In burnProducts, the ID is computed from only products[i].products[0] even when vault.burnBatch burns multiple products. The code adds _positions[id] to totalPositions and then immediately deletes _positions[id]. If multiple products with the same ID are burned (either in the same batch or in separate calls), only the first burn includes the aggregated cost basis in totalPositions; subsequent burns see _positions[id] == 0. Their full proceeds are then treated as pure profit, charged a fee, and added to totalCollateral via totalEarned > totalPositions. This inflates totalCollateral without a corresponding increase in net assets. An attacker can deposit to obtain shares, trigger burns of multiple positions with the same ID or a multi-product batch, inflate totalCollateral, and then withdraw and claim redemptions at the inflated share price, draining collateral from other shareholders. This is directly exploitable and severe.

code: function mintProducts( ProductMint[] calldata products, bytes calldata signature ) external { bytes32 signatures; for (uint256 i = 0; i < products.length; i++) { require(vaults[products[i].vault], "Automator: invalid vault"); IVault(products[i].vault).mint( products[i].totalCollateral, products[i].mintParams, referral ); bytes32 id = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(products[i].vault, products[i].mintParams.expiry, products[i].mintParams.anchorPrices)); _positions[id] = _positions[id] + products[i].totalCollateral - products[i].mintParams.makerCollateral; signatures = signatures ^ keccak256(products[i].mintParams.makerSignature); } (address signer, ) = signatures.toEthSignedMessageHash().tryRecover(signature); require(makers[signer], "Automator: invalid maker"); require(collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) >= totalPendingRedemptions * getPricePerShare() / 1e18, "Automator: no enough collateral to redeem"); emit ProductsMinted(products); }
vulnerability: XOR signature aggregation allows replay/duplication of valid mint authorizations
reason: The batch authorization is computed as the XOR of keccak256(makerSignature) for each product. XOR is commutative and associative, and duplicate elements cancel in pairs. An attacker who observes a valid mint transaction with a single product and its makerSignature hash h and outer signature sig over h can submit an array containing three identical copies of that ProductMint. The XOR of three identical hashes is h ^ h ^ h = h, so the same outer signature sig remains valid. Each loop iteration calls vault.mint, causing the Automator to spend collateral multiple times for the same authorized mint. Because MintParams contains no nonce and the Automator does not check for duplicate products or replay, an attacker can repeat this with any odd number of copies (1 + 2k). This can force the Automator to mint excessive positions, potentially draining its collateral into risky or worthless positions. The flaw is exploitable by anyone with access to a valid maker signature and can lead to significant loss of funds.

code: function initialize( address collateral_, address referral_, address feeCollector_ ) external initializer { collateral = IERC20(collateral_); referral = referral_; feeCollector = feeCollector_; __Ownable_init(); __ERC1155Holder_init(); __ERC20_init( string(abi.encodePacked("Automator ", IERC20Metadata(collateral_).name())), string(abi.encodePacked("at", IERC20Metadata(collateral_).symbol())) ); }
vulnerability: Unprotected initializer can be front-run to take ownership and drain funds
reason: The initialize function is external and only guarded by the initializer modifier. There is no constructor or _disableInitializers() call for the implementation, and no guarantee that deployment and initialization occur in the same transaction. An attacker can front-run the legitimate initialization by calling initialize with their own collateral_, referral_, and feeCollector_ addresses. This sets the attacker as the owner via __Ownable_init(). As owner, the attacker can call enableVaults to approve a malicious vault with type(uint256).max allowance, enable themselves as a maker, and then use mintProducts or the malicious vault to transfer all deposited collateral out of the contract. They can also set feeCollector to themselves. This is a classic uninitialized initializer vulnerability and is directly exploitable in real-world deployments that do not atomically initialize the proxy.
